page.layout: One block of verse in the centre of the page, with a signature and date below it right-aligned, then a printer's ornament at the foot. No running head, no page number, no margin notes.

main_text.p: Propositi archetypum celebri GENATHIUS arte Gestit solemni distribuisse foro.
Gaudete Astraea soboles dilecta, Heliconi Hoc opere insignis conciliatur honos.
Exoptata dies cum nos veneranda Geneva Contubernales vellet habere suos.
Exoptata dies, cum nostra antiqua Nemausus In viridi audiret plectra Daphnone Lyra.
Et cum trans Gardi triplicem nos Utica pontem Exciperet, Musis Utica amica meis.
Quam mihi SANRAVI gratum coluisse Penates, Atque inter Charites vivere Monspelii!
O utinam divina meas Hygiea Camenas Aspiciat, morbos impediatque novos!
Quinque per hos menses miserè me exercuit ægrum Gutta per articulos præcipitata meos.
Frigidus heu stomachus, calidum jecur, atque cerebrum Debile, sunt vitæ carnificina meæ!
Nunc mihi subducit vires, nunc reddit easdem: Me DEUS horrisono servat in Oceano.
Illius arbitrio sto, surgo, cadoque, beatis Donec tandem etiam me inserat ordinibus.

page.notes: The verse is set in italic with some words in roman capitals and small capitals; the signature line is in spaced capitals. Abbreviations such as "arte~", "pontem~", "eastdem~" and "atq;" are rendered as printed with the tilde or q-mark; the marks over "Quinq" and "Quinq;" are read as the abbreviation for -que. Some letter forms ("Quam", "Propositi") are uncertain in the scan. The date line "II.Febr.1627." is shown with the numeral form as printed. The ornament at the foot is not transcribed.
